description: Coordinate Geometry is a vital combination of Algebra and Geometry. In this branch of mathematics, the position of points on a plane is represented as a pair of numbers, known as coordinates.

sections.title: Cartesian System and Distance Formula
sections.description: This section focuses on the basic principles of representing points on a plane and calculating the distance between them.

key_concepts.explanation: The point where the X-axis and Y-axis intersect each other.
The coordinate axes divide the plane into four parts, called Quadrants. The signs are (+,+), (-,+), (-,-), and (+,-) respectively.

results: If three points A, B, and C are collinear, the sum of any two distances is equal to the third. (e.g., AB + BC = AC)

sections.title: Section Formula
sections.description: This section explains the method to find the coordinates of a point that divides a line segment in a given ratio.

results: If the value of k is negative, the division is external.

sections.title: Area of a Triangle
sections.description: The formula to calculate the area of a triangle formed by three given vertices in Coordinate Geometry.

key_concepts.explanation: Since area can never be negative, the absolute value of the calculated result is taken.

sections.title: Slope of a Line
sections.description: The method of measuring the inclination of a line, known as its slope or gradient.

equations: m = tan(θ) (where θ is the angle with the X-axis)

key_concepts.explanation: It indicates how steep a line is and its direction.

results: m1 = m2 (Slopes of both lines are equal)
m1 * m2 = -1 (Product of their slopes is -1)

sections.title: Equations of a Line
sections.description: Various methods to express a straight line algebraically based on different given conditions.

equations: y - y1 = ((y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)) * (x - x1) (Two-Point Form)

steps.title: Find the Slope
steps.detail: If two points are given, first calculate the slope using the formula m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1).

steps.title: Apply the Equation
steps.detail: Using the slope (m) and any one point (x1, y1), substitute the values into the Point-Slope Form to get the equation of the line.
